cues.zh: 所以，我想请大家先设想一下
cues.en: So, I'd like you to imagine for a moment

cues.zh: 你是一名身处激战中的士兵。
cues.en: that you are a soldier in the heat of battle.

cues.zh: 也许你是罗马步兵，或是中世纪弓箭手
cues.en: Maybe you're a Roman foot soldier or a medieval archer

cues.zh: 又或者你是祖鲁战士。
cues.en: or maybe you're a Zulu warrior.

cues.zh: 无论你身处哪个时代、哪个地方，
cues.en: Regardless of your time and place,

cues.zh: 有些东西是恒定不变的。
cues.en: there are some things that are constant.

cues.zh: 你的肾上腺素飙升，你的行动源自
cues.en: Your adrenaline is elevated, and your actions are stemming

cues.zh: 这些根深蒂固的反射。
cues.en: from these deeply ingrained reflexes.

cues.zh: 这些反射源于保护自己和己方的需要
cues.en: Reflexes rooted in a need to protect yourself and your side

cues.zh: 以及击败敌人。
cues.en: and to defeat the enemy.

cues.zh: 那么现在，我想请大家设想扮演一个截然不同的角色。
cues.en: So now I'd like you to imagine playing a very different role.

cues.zh: 侦察兵。
cues.en: That of the scout.

cues.zh: 侦察兵的职责不是进攻或防守。
cues.en: So the scout's job is not to attack or defend.

cues.zh: 侦察兵的职责是去理解。
cues.en: The scout's job is to understand.

cues.zh: 侦察兵是那个走出去的人，
cues.en: The scout is the one going out,

cues.zh: 绘制地形、识别潜在障碍，
cues.en: mapping the terrain, identifying potential obstacles,

cues.zh: 而侦察兵或许希望了解到，比如说，有一座桥
cues.en: and the scout may hope to learn that say, there's a bridge

cues.zh: 正好位于过河的便利位置。
cues.en: in a convenient location across the river.

cues.zh: 最重要的是，侦察兵想知道那里究竟有什么
cues.en: But above all, the scout wants to know what's really there

cues.zh: 尽可能准确。
cues.en: as accurately as possible.

cues.zh: 而在真正的军队中，
cues.en: And in a real actual army,

cues.zh: 士兵和侦察兵都必不可少。
cues.en: both the soldier and the scout are essential.

cues.zh: 但你也可以把这两种角色看作两种思维模式。
cues.en: But you can also think of each of these roles as a mindset.

cues.zh: 一个比喻，说明我们所有人如何加工信息
cues.en: A metaphor for how all of us process information

cues.zh: 和日常生活中的想法。
cues.en: and ideas in our daily lives.

cues.zh: 我今天要论证的是，拥有良好的判断力、
cues.en: And what I'm going to argue today is that having good judgment,

cues.zh: 做出准确的预测、做出好的决定
cues.en: and making accurate predictions, making good decisions

cues.zh: 主要取决于你处于哪种思维模式。
cues.en: is mostly about which mindset you're in.

cues.zh: 那么，为了说明这些思维模式的运作，
cues.en: So, to illustrate these mindsets in action,

cues.zh: 我要带你们回到19世纪的法国
cues.en: I'm going to take you back to 19th century France

cues.zh: 在那里，这张看似无害的纸引发
cues.en: where this innocuous looking piece of paper launched

cues.zh: 了历史上最大的政治丑闻之一。
cues.en: one of the biggest political scandals in history.

cues.zh: 它于1894年被发现，发现者是
cues.en: It was discovered in 1894 by officers

cues.zh: 法国总参谋部的军官们。
cues.en: in the French general staff.

cues.zh: 它在一只废纸篓里被撕碎了
cues.en: And it was torn up in a wastepaper basket

cues.zh: 但当他们把它拼回去时，他们发现
cues.en: but when they pieced it back together, they discovered

cues.zh: 他们内部有人一直在出售军事机密
cues.en: that someone in their ranks had been selling military secrets

cues.zh: 给德国。
cues.en: to Germany.

cues.zh: 于是他们展开了大规模调查
cues.en: So they launched a big investigation

cues.zh: 而他们的怀疑很快集中
cues.en: and their suspicions quickly converged

cues.zh: 到了这个人身上，阿尔弗雷德·德雷福斯。
cues.en: on this man, Alfred Dreyfus.

cues.zh: 他的履历无可挑剔。
cues.en: He had a sterling record.

cues.zh: 没有过往的不当行为记录，
cues.en: No past history of wrongdoing,

cues.zh: 据他们所知也没有动机。
cues.en: no motive as far as they could tell.

cues.zh: 但德雷福斯是军中该军衔唯一的犹太裔军官
cues.en: But Dreyfus was the only Jewish officer at that rank in the Army

cues.zh: 不幸的是，在当时
cues.en: and unfortunately, at this time,

cues.zh: 法国军队反犹情绪极为严重。
cues.en: the French army was highly anti-semitic.

cues.zh: 于是他们把德雷福斯的笔迹与备忘录上的笔迹作比对
cues.en: So they compared Dreyfus's handwriting to that on the memo

cues.zh: 并认定两者相符。
cues.en: and included that it was a match.

cues.zh: 尽管外部的专业笔迹专家
cues.en: Even though outside professional handwriting experts

cues.zh: 对相似度的把握要低得多，但先不管这个。
cues.en: were much less confident in the similarity, but never mind that.

cues.zh: 他们去搜查了德雷福斯的公寓
cues.en: They went and searched Dreyfus's apartment

cues.zh: 寻找任何间谍活动的迹象。
cues.en: looking for any signs of espionage.

cues.zh: 他们翻遍了他的文件，却一无所获。
cues.en: They went through his files and they didn't find anything.

cues.zh: 而这反而让他们更加确信，德雷福斯不仅有罪，
cues.en: And this just convinced them more that Dreyfus was not only guilty,

cues.zh: 而且还很狡猾，因为显然他早已把所有证据都藏了起来，
cues.en: but sneaky as well, because clearly he had hidden all of the evidence

cues.zh: 赶在他们找到之前。
cues.en: before they had managed to get to it.

cues.zh: 接着，他们又去翻查了他的个人历史
cues.en: Next, they went and looked through his personal history

cues.zh: 寻找任何能定罪的细节。
cues.en: for any incriminating details.

cues.zh: 他们和他的老师们谈过。
cues.en: They talked to his teachers.

cues.zh: 他们发现他在学校学过外语
cues.en: They found that he had studied foreign languages in school

cues.zh: 这显然表明他有与外国政府勾结的意图
cues.en: which clearly showed a desire to conspire with foreign governments

cues.zh: 在日后的人生中。
cues.en: later in life.

cues.zh: 他的老师们还说，德雷福斯记性很好
cues.en: His teachers also said that Dreyfus had a good memory

cues.zh: 并以记性好而闻名。
cues.en: and was known for having a good memory.

cues.zh: 这非常可疑，对吧？
cues.en: Which was highly suspicious, right?

cues.zh: 你知道，因为间谍得记住很多东西。
cues.en: You know, because a spy has to remember a lot of things.

cues.zh: 于是，案件开庭审理，德雷福斯被判有罪。
cues.en: So, the case went to trial and Dreyfus was found guilty.

cues.zh: 之后，他们把他带到这个公共广场上
cues.en: And afterwards they took him out into this public square

cues.zh: 仪式性地撕掉他制服上的徽章
cues.en: and ritualistically tore his insignia for his uniform

cues.zh: 并将他的佩剑折成两段。
cues.en: and broke his sword and two.

cues.zh: 这被称为德雷福斯的降级仪式。
cues.en: This is called the degradation of Dreyfus.

cues.zh: 他们判处他终身监禁
cues.en: And they sentenced him to life imprisonment

cues.zh: 关押在名字恰如其分的魔鬼岛
cues.en: on the aptly named Devil's Island

cues.zh: 那是南美洲海岸外一块荒芜的岩石。
cues.en: which is this barren rock off the coast of South America.

cues.zh: 他就这样去了那里。
cues.en: So there he went.

cues.zh: 在那里，他独自度日，写信
cues.en: And there he spent his days alone writing letters

cues.zh: 一封又一封地写给法国政府
cues.en: and letters to the French government

cues.zh: 恳求他们重审他的案子，以便发现他的清白。
cues.en: begging them to reopen his case so they could discover his innocence.

cues.zh: 但大多数情况下，法国认为此事已经了结。
cues.en: But for the most part, France considered the matter closed.

cues.zh: 所以对我来说，德雷福斯事件中
cues.en: So one thing that's really interesting to me

cues.zh: 真正有趣的一点是这个问题：
cues.en: about the Dreyfus Affair is this question

cues.zh: 为什么那些军官如此确信
cues.en: of why the officers were so convinced

cues.zh: 德雷福斯有罪。
cues.en: that Dreyfus was guilty.

cues.zh: 甚至可能以为他们是给他设了套。
cues.en: I mean you might even assume that they were setting him up.

cues.zh: 他们是在故意陷害他，
cues.en: They were intentionally framing him,

cues.zh: 但历史学家认为事实并非如此。
cues.en: but historians don't think that's what happened.

cues.zh: 就我们所能判断的，那些军官真心相信
cues.en: As far as we can tell, the officers genuinely believed

cues.zh: 对德雷福斯的指控是确凿的。
cues.en: that the case against Dreyfus was strong.

cues.zh: 这就让人不禁想问，
cues.en: Which you know, makes you wonder what does it say

cues.zh: 人类心智到底是怎么回事，竟会把如此微不足道的证据
cues.en: about the human mind that we can find such paltry evidence

cues.zh: 当成足以定一个人罪的铁证？
cues.en: to be compelling enough to convict a man?

cues.zh: 这就是科学家所说的
cues.en: Well, this is a case of what scientists call

cues.zh: “动机性推理”。
cues.en: "motivated reasoning".

cues.zh: 就是这种现像：我们无意识的动机、
cues.en: It's this phenomenon which our unconscious motivations,

cues.zh: 欲望和恐惧，塑造了我们解读信息的方式。
cues.en: our desires and fears shape the way we interpret information.

cues.zh: 于是有些信息、有些观念感觉像是我们的盟友，
cues.en: So some information, some ideas feel like our allies

cues.zh: 我们希望它们赢。
cues.en: and we want them to win.

cues.zh: 我们想捍卫它们。
cues.en: We want to defend them.

cues.zh: 而另一些信息或观念则是敌人，
cues.en: And other information or ideas are the enemy

cues.zh: 我们想把它们击落。
cues.en: and we want to shoot them down.

cues.zh: 所以这就是为什么我把动机性推理称为“士兵思维”。
cues.en: So this is why I call motivated reasoning, "soldier mindset."

cues.zh: 你们大多数人应该都没迫害过
cues.en: And probably most of you have never persecuted

cues.zh: 一位法国犹太裔军官，指控他叛国吧，我猜，
cues.en: a French Jewish officer for high treason I assume,

cues.zh: 但你们可能关注过体育或政治。
cues.en: but maybe you've followed sports or politics.

cues.zh: 所以你也许注意到，当裁判判定
cues.en: So you might have noticed that when the referee judges

cues.zh: 比如你的队伍犯规时，
cues.en: that your team committed a foul for example,

cues.zh: 你会非常有动力去找出他判错的理由。
cues.en: you're highly motivated to find reasons why he's wrong.

cues.zh: 但如果他判定对方队伍犯规——太棒了！
cues.en: But if he judges that the other team committed a foul - awesome!

cues.zh: 判得好。
cues.en: That's a good call.

cues.zh: 咱们就别细究了。
cues.en: Let's not examine it too closely.

cues.zh: 或者，你可能读过一篇文章或研究，
cues.en: Or, maybe you've read an article or study

cues.zh: 探讨某个有争议的政策，
cues.en: that examined some controversial policy

cues.zh: 比如死刑。
cues.en: like capital punishment.

cues.zh: 正如研究人员已经证实的，
cues.en: And as researchers have demonstrated,

cues.zh: 如果你支持死刑，
cues.en: if you support capital punishment,

cues.zh: 而研究表明死刑并不有效，
cues.en: and the study shows that is not effective,

cues.zh: 那你就会非常有动力去找出所有理由，
cues.en: then you're highly motivated to find all the reasons

cues.zh: 证明这项研究设计得很糟糕。
cues.en: why the study was poorly designed.

cues.zh: 但如果研究表明死刑有效——那太好了！
cues.en: But if it shows that capital punishment works - awesome!

cues.zh: 这是一项好研究。反之亦然。
cues.en: It's a good study. And vice versa.

cues.zh: 如果你不支持死刑，也是一样。
cues.en: If you don't support capital punishment, same thing.

cues.zh: 我们的判断只是被无意识地强烈影响
cues.en: Our judgment is just strongly influenced unconsciously

cues.zh: 被我们想赢的那一方。
cues.en: by which side we want to win.

cues.zh: 而这无处不在。
cues.en: And this is ubiquitous.

cues.zh: 这塑造了我们如何看待健康、人际关系，
cues.en: This shapes how we think about our health, relationships,

cues.zh: 如何决定投票，我们认为什么是公平或道德的，
cues.en: how we decide how to vote, what we consider fair or ethical,

cues.zh: 而对我来说，动机性推理
cues.en: and what's most scary to me about motivated reasoning

cues.zh: 或士兵心态最可怕的地方，是它有多么无意识。
cues.en: or soldier mindset, is how unconscious it is.

cues.zh: 我们可以认为自己客观公正
cues.en: We can think we're being objective and fair-minded

cues.zh: 却最终还是毁了一个无辜者的人生。
cues.en: and still wind up ruining the life of an innocent man.

cues.zh: 然而，幸运的是，对德雷福斯来说，他的故事还没有结束。
cues.en: However, fortunately for Dreyfus, his story is not over.

cues.zh: 这位是皮卡尔上校。
cues.en: This is Colonel Picquart.

cues.zh: 他是法国军队的另一位高级军官，
cues.en: He is another high-ranking officer in the French army,

cues.zh: 和大多数人一样，他认定德雷福斯有罪。
cues.en: and like most people, he assumed Dreyfus was guilty.

cues.zh: 和军队里大多数人一样，
cues.en: Also like most people in the Army,

cues.zh: 他至少也随口反犹。
cues.en: he was at least casually anti-Semitic.

cues.zh: 但到了某个节点，Picquart 开始怀疑，
cues.en: But at a certain point, Picquart began to suspect

cues.zh: 万一我们对 Dreyfus 的判断全错了呢？
cues.en: what if we are all wrong about Dreyfus?

cues.zh: 事情是这样的，他发现了证据，
cues.en: And what happened was, he had discovered evidence

cues.zh: 证明为德国从事间谍活动的行为仍在继续，
cues.en: that the spying for Germany had continued

cues.zh: 即便 Dreyfus 已经入狱。
cues.en: even after Dreyfus was in prison.

cues.zh: 他还发现军队里另一名军官
cues.en: And he had also discovered that another officer in the Army

cues.zh: 的笔迹与那份备忘录完全吻合。
cues.en: had handwriting that perfectly matched the memo.

cues.zh: 比 Dreyfus 的笔迹接近得多。
cues.en: Much closer than Dreyfus's handwriting.

cues.zh: 于是他把这些发现呈报给上级，
cues.en: So he brought these discoveries to his superiors

cues.zh: 但令他沮丧的是，他们要么毫不在意，
cues.en: but to his dismay, they either didn't care,

cues.zh: 要么编出一套套精巧的说辞来解释他的发现，
cues.en: or came up with elaborate rationalizations to explain his findings,

cues.zh: 比如：“Piquart，你真正证明的只是另有一名间谍
cues.en: like, "Well, all you've really shown, Piquart, is that there is another spy

cues.zh: 学会了模仿 Dreyfus 的笔迹，
cues.en: who learned how to mimic Dreyfus's handwriting,

cues.zh: 在 Dreyfus 离开后接过了间谍的接力棒。”
cues.en: and he picked up the torch of spying after Dreyfus left.

cues.zh: 但德雷福斯仍然有罪。
cues.en: But Dreyfus is still guilty.

cues.zh: 最终，皮卡尔成功为德雷福斯洗清了罪名。
cues.en: Eventually, Piquart managed to get Dreyfus exonerated.

cues.zh: 但这花了他10年时间，
cues.en: But it took him 10 years,

cues.zh: 而且其中一段时间，他自己还身陷囹圄，
cues.en: and for part of that time, he himself was in prison

cues.zh: 罪名是对军队不忠。
cues.en: for the crime of disloyalty to the Army.

cues.zh: 所以，你知道，很多人觉得
cues.en: So, you know, a lot of people feel

cues.zh: 皮卡尔实在算不上这个故事里的英雄。
cues.en: like Piquart can't really be the hero of this story.

cues.zh: 因为他是个反犹分子，这很糟糕。
cues.en: Because he was an anti-Semite and that's bad.

cues.zh: 这一点我同意，但就我个人而言，
cues.en: Which I agree with, but personally, for me,

cues.zh: 皮卡尔反犹这一事实
cues.en: the fact that Piquant was anti-Semitic

cues.zh: 反而让我觉得他的行为更加令人敬佩。
cues.en: actually makes his actions more admirable to me.

cues.zh: 因为他有着和其他军官一样的偏见、一样的理由
cues.en: Because he had the same prejudices, the same reasons

cues.zh: 去抱有偏颇，
cues.en: to be biased as his fellow officers,

cues.zh: 但他追寻真相并坚守真相的动机，压倒了这一切。
cues.en: but his motivation to find the truth and uphold it just trumped all of that.

cues.zh: 所以对我来说，
cues.en: So to me,

cues.zh: 皮卡尔是我所谓的“侦察兵思维”的典范。
cues.en: Piquart is a poster child for what I call "scout mindset."

cues.zh: 这种驱动力不是要让某个观点赢或另一个输，
cues.en: It's the drive not to make one idea win or another lose,

cues.zh: 而只是尽可能诚实、准确地看清事物的真相，
cues.en: but just to see what's really there as honestly and accurately as you can,

cues.zh: 即使它并不美好、并不方便、也并不令人愉快。
cues.en: even if it's not pretty or convenient or pleasant.

cues.zh: 这种心态正是我个人热衷的。
cues.en: And this mindset is what I'm personally passionate about.

cues.zh: 也是我过去几年一直在研究的
cues.en: And what I've spent the last few years examining

cues.zh: 试图弄清楚是什么造就了侦察兵心态。
cues.en: and trying to figure out what causes scout mindset.

cues.zh: 你知道，为什么有些人至少有时候
cues.en: You know, why are some people sometimes at least,

cues.zh: 能够突破自己的偏见、偏误和动机
cues.en: able to cut through their own prejudices and biases and motivations

cues.zh: 只是去看事实和证据
cues.en: and just to see the facts and evidence

cues.zh: 尽可能客观地看？
cues.en: as objectively as they can?

cues.zh: 答案是情感层面的。
cues.en: And the answer is emotional.

cues.zh: 所以，正如士兵心态植根于情感
cues.en: So, just as the soldier mindset is rooted in emotions

cues.zh: 比如防御心理或部落主义，侦察兵心态也是如此。
cues.en: like defensiveness or tribalism, scout mindset is too.

cues.zh: 只是植根于不同的情感。
cues.en: It's just rooted in different emotions.

cues.zh: 比如，侦察兵充满好奇。
cues.en: So for example, scouts are curious.

cues.zh: 他们更可能说自己感到愉悦
cues.en: They're more likely to say that they feel pleasure

cues.zh: 当学到新信息时，或者有种想解开谜题的冲动。
cues.en: when they learn new information or an itch to solve a puzzle.

cues.zh: 他们更可能感到着迷
cues.en: They're more likely to feel intrigued

cues.zh: 当遇到与预期相矛盾的事物时。
cues.en: when they encounter something that contradicts or expectations.

cues.zh: 侦察者也有不同的价值观。
cues.en: Scouts also have different values.

cues.zh: 他们更可能认为检验自己的信念是一种美德，
cues.en: They are more likely to say that they think it's virtuous

cues.zh: 而他们不太会说
cues.en: to test your own beliefs and they're less likely to say

cues.zh: 改变主意的人显得软弱。
cues.en: that someone who changes his mind seems weak.

cues.zh: 最重要的是，侦察者脚踏实地。
cues.en: And above all, scouts are grounded.

cues.zh: 这意味着他们作为人的自我价值
cues.en: Which means that their self-worth

cues.zh: 并不取决于他们在任何特定话题上
cues.en: as a person isn't tied to how right or wrong they are

cues.zh: 是对还是错。
cues.en: about any particular topic.

cues.zh: 所以，他们可以相信死刑有效，
cues.en: So, you know, they can believe that capital punishment works

cues.zh: 而如果研究显示死刑无效，他们可以说：
cues.en: and if studies come out showing that it doesn't, they can say,

cues.zh: “嗯，看来我可能错了。
cues.en: "Huh. Looks like I might be wrong.

cues.zh: 这不意味着我不好或愚蠢。”
cues.en: Doesn't mean I'm bad or stupid."

cues.zh: 所以这些特质，这一组特质，
cues.en: So these traits, this cluster of traits

cues.zh: 是研究人员发现的——
cues.en: is what researchers have found -

cues.zh: 我也从轶事中发现了——能预测良好判断力的特质。
cues.en: and I've also found anecdotally - predicts good judgment.

cues.zh: 我想留给你的关键要点
cues.en: And the key takeaway I want to leave you with

cues.zh: 关于这些特质，是它们主要
cues.en: about those traits is that they're primarily

cues.zh: 不在于你有多聪明，或者你知道多少。
cues.en: not about how smart you are, or about how much you know.

cues.zh: 事实上，它们和智商几乎没什么关联。
cues.en: In fact they don't correlate very much with IQ at all.

cues.zh: 它们关乎的是你的感受。
cues.en: They're about how you feel.

cues.zh: 我一直反复回味圣-埃克苏佩里的一句话。
cues.en: So, there's a quote that I keep coming back to by Saint-Exupery.

cues.zh: 他是《小王子》的作者。
cues.en: He is the author of "The Little Prince."

cues.zh: 他说：“如果你想造一艘船，
cues.en: And he said, "If you want to build a ship,

cues.zh: 不要鼓动人们去收集木材、发号施令，
cues.en: don't drum up your men to collect wood and give orders

cues.zh: 分配任务。
cues.en: and distribute the work.

cues.zh: 而是教他们渴望那片浩瀚无垠的大海。”
cues.en: Instead, teach them to yearn for the vast and endless sea."

cues.zh: 换句话说，我认为如果我们想
cues.en: In other words, I claim if we want

cues.zh: 真正提升个人和社会的判断力，
cues.en: to really improve our judgment as individuals and as societies,

cues.zh: 我们最需要的不是更多逻辑学或修辞学的教导，
cues.en: what we need most is not more instruction in logic or rhetoric

cues.zh: 也不是概率论或经济学，
cues.en: or probability or economics,

cues.zh: 尽管那些东西都很有价值。
cues.en: even though those things are quite valuable.

cues.zh: 但要善用这些原则，
cues.en: But what we most need

cues.zh: 我们最需要的是侦察兵心态。
cues.en: to use those principles well, is scout mindset.

cues.zh: 我们需要改变自己的感受方式。
cues.en: We need to change the way we feel.

cues.zh: 我们需要学会感到自豪而非羞愧，
cues.en: We need to learn how to feel proud instead of ashamed

cues.zh: 当我们发现自己可能在某件事上错了的时候。
cues.en: when we notice we might have been wrong about something.

cues.zh: 我们需要学会在遇到与信念相悖的信息时，感到好奇而不是防御。
cues.en: We need to learn how to feel intrigued instead of defensive

cues.zh: 当我们遇到一些信息
cues.en: when we encounter some information

cues.zh: 与我们的信念相矛盾时。
cues.en: that contradicts our beliefs.

cues.zh: 所以，我想留给你的问题是，
cues.en: So, the question I want to leave you with,

cues.zh: 你最渴望的是什么？
cues.en: is what do you most yearn for?

cues.zh: 你渴望捍卫自己的信念，
cues.en: Do you yearn to defend your own beliefs,

cues.zh: 还是渴望尽可能清晰地看清这个世界？
cues.en: or do you yearn to see the world as clearly as you possibly can?

cues.zh: 谢谢。
cues.en: Thank you.
